# LSS: primary Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS benchmark

The two LSS methods are **distinct interventions on distinct populations**, not
interchangeable estimates of the same thing:

- **Na/K–SBP (primary)** models sodium displacement **and** potassium addition
  through SBP, affecting **all four CVD causes**; it applies to whole-population
  (s2) and to NCD-RisC diagnosed/treated hypertensives (s4/s5).
- **SSaSS trial-RR (benchmark)** applies the SSaSS **stroke** relative risks
  (incidence + case fatality) and is valid only for SSaSS-comparable
  (diagnosed/treated HTN) populations — never the whole population.

```{r nak-vs-ssass, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Deaths delayed by scenario (impact window) joined to the LSS audit composition,
# for the HTN variants where both methods exist.
dd_lss <- deaths_delayed_by(data.out, by = character(0), years = impact_y1:impact_y2)
dd_lss <- dd_lss[grepl("^lss", as.character(scenario)),
                 .(scenario = as.character(scenario), deaths_delayed)]
la <- as.data.table(lss_audit)
la_sc <- la[, .(elig = eligibility_group[1], cov = mean(eligible_pop_share),
                na_disp = mean(sodium_displaced_g), k_add = mean(potassium_added_g),
                dsbp = mean(sbp_delta_combined_mmHg)), by = .(scenario, method)]
cmp <- merge(la_sc, dd_lss, by = "scenario", all.x = TRUE)
cmp[, `:=`(Scenario = scenario_labels[scenario])]
setorder(cmp, method, scenario)
cmp_tbl <- cmp[, .(
  Scenario, Method = method, `Eligibility` = elig,
  `Elig. pop share` = fmt_pct(cov, 1),
  `Na displaced (g)` = formatC(na_disp, format = "f", digits = 3),
  `K increase (g)`   = formatC(k_add,   format = "f", digits = 3),
  `Mean ΔSBP (mmHg)` = ifelse(is.na(dsbp), "n/a (trial RR)", formatC(dsbp, format = "f", digits = 2)),
  `Deaths delayed (M)` = ifelse(is.na(deaths_delayed), "n/a", fmt_m(deaths_delayed)))]
kable(cmp_tbl, caption = paste0("Table 3b. LSS Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS trial-RR ",
      "benchmark: eligibility, exposure change, SBP change and deaths delayed ",
      "(", impact_window, "). The methods are NOT identical interventions — they ",
      "differ in pathway (all-CVD SBP vs stroke-only RR) and are shown side by side, ",
      "not merged."),
      align = c("l","l","l", rep("r",5))) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = TRUE, font_size = 11) |>
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
  footnote(general = paste0(
    "ΔSBP is 'n/a (trial RR)' for the SSaSS benchmark because its effect is a ",
    "stroke relative risk, not an SBP change. Na displaced / K increase are the ",
    "same composition for both methods; the health effect differs by pathway."))
```

# Benchmarking against the "100 Million Lives Saved" model {#benchmarking}

As an external sanity check, we compare this build's headline result — the
**full package** of sodium policies — against the previous RTSL/UW
**"100 Million Lives Saved"** estimate for a **30% reduction in population
sodium intake**. The previous-model figures are read from
[`data/raw/UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx`](../data/raw/UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx)
(sheet `Location And Cause`, intervention `Population Sodium Reduction`). The
comparison is restricted to the **same selected countries** this report models,
so it tracks the country selection automatically.

**This is a contextual comparison, not a like-for-like validation.** The two
estimates are close in construction but *not* equivalent, and we do not adjust
either to force agreement:

- **Exposure change differs.** The previous scenario applies a **uniform 30%
  cut to all population sodium**. The current full package applies each policy's
  documented effect **only to the sodium sources it can reach** (public
  procurement + FOPL + salt targets + fiscal), giving a country-specific
  total-intake reduction (`salteff`) that is generally **well below 30%**. The
  current package is therefore expected to delay **fewer** deaths than a flat
  30% cut — the gap is a feature of the policy-reach logic, not an error.
- **Outcome & causes.** Both report **deaths delayed** relative to a
  no-intervention baseline over the same four CVD causes (IHD, ischemic stroke,
  intracerebral hemorrhage, HHD), so the outcome definition is aligned.
- **Baselines & horizon differ.** The two models use different baseline death
  counts (different populations, age ranges and projection horizons), so we
  report deaths delayed both in **absolute** terms and as a **percent of each
  model's own baseline** — the percent is the more comparable metric. The
  previous model's cumulative horizon is close to, but not identical to, this
  build's `r impact_window` window.
- **Country names** are harmonised onto this model's spellings before matching
  (all ten priority countries match exactly; e.g. `Viet Nam`).

```{r benchmark-compute, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# ---- Benchmark: current full package vs 100M-Lives 30% sodium reduction ------
# Previous-model results live in the 100 Million Lives Saved workbook, sheet
# "Location And Cause". The comparison row is the "Population Sodium Reduction"
# intervention, which in that model represents the WHO 30%-relative-reduction
# sodium target. We compare it to THIS build's full package (reusing dd_country
# computed above; the model itself is never re-run here).
PREV_XLSX       <- paste0(wd_raw, "UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx")
PREV_SHEET      <- "Location And Cause"
PREV_SODIUM_INT <- "Population Sodium Reduction"   # = 30% population sodium reduction

# Harmonise previous-model country names onto this model's spellings. The ten
# priority countries already match; this guards other spellings for robustness.
harmonize_prev_location <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[x == "Vietnam"]                  <- "Viet Nam"
  x[x == "United States of America"] <- "United States"
  x
}

# Current model: full-package deaths delayed by country over the impact window.
bench_current <- dd_country[, .(location,
                                dd_current   = deaths_delayed,
                                base_current = baseline_dead)]

# Selected countries = whatever the model was run for; the benchmark filters the
# previous-model table to exactly these, so it updates with the selection.
sel_countries <- sort(unique(as.character(bench_current$location)))

benchmark <- tryCatch({
  prev <- as.data.table(readxl::read_excel(PREV_XLSX, sheet = PREV_SHEET))
  prev[, location := harmonize_prev_location(location)]
  prev <- prev[intervention == PREV_SODIUM_INT & location %in% sel_countries,
               .(location,
                 dd_prev   = as.numeric(deaths_delayed),
                 base_prev = as.numeric(baseline_deaths))]
  b <- merge(bench_current, prev, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)
  b[, `:=`(pct_current = dd_current / base_current,
           pct_prev    = dd_prev    / base_prev,
           ratio       = dd_current / dd_prev)]
  setorder(b, -dd_prev)
  b[]
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Benchmark workbook could not be read: ", conditionMessage(e))
  NULL
})

benchmark_available <- !is.null(benchmark) && nrow(benchmark) > 0 &&
  any(!is.na(benchmark$dd_prev))

# Selected-country totals (used inline, in the deck bundle, and for the plot).
if (benchmark_available) {
  bench_cur_tot   <- sum(benchmark$dd_current, na.rm = TRUE)
  bench_prev_tot  <- sum(benchmark$dd_prev,    na.rm = TRUE)
  bench_ratio_tot <- bench_cur_tot / bench_prev_tot
} else {
  bench_cur_tot <- bench_prev_tot <- bench_ratio_tot <- NA_real_
}

# Long form for the grouped bar plot (built once, reused by the deck export).
bench_model_labs <- c(dd_current = "Current full package",
                      dd_prev    = "Previous 30% sodium reduction")
bench_cols <- c(`Current full package`         = "#1f78b4",
                `Previous 30% sodium reduction` = "#b2182b")
if (benchmark_available) {
  bench_long <- melt(benchmark[, .(location, dd_current, dd_prev)],
                     id.vars = "location", variable.name = "model",
                     value.name = "dd")
  bench_long[, model := factor(bench_model_labs[as.character(model)],
                               levels = unname(bench_model_labs))]
  bench_long <- bench_long[!is.na(dd)]
} else {
  bench_long <- NULL
}
```

```{r benchmark-availability-note, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!benchmark_available)
  cat("**Benchmark workbook unavailable — the comparison below is skipped.** ",
      "Place `UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx` in `data/raw/` and re-knit.\n")
```

Over `r impact_window`, across the `r length(sel_countries)` selected countries,
the current **full package** delays **`r fmt_m(bench_cur_tot)` million** CVD
deaths, versus **`r fmt_m(bench_prev_tot)` million** for the previous flat-30%
sodium-reduction scenario — a ratio of about
**`r formatC(bench_ratio_tot, format = "f", digits = 2)`×**. The current
package delivering a smaller total is expected: its source-limited `salteff` is
generally well below a uniform 30% intake cut.

## Benchmark table

```{r benchmark-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
if (benchmark_available) {
  bt  <- copy(benchmark)
  setorder(bt, -dd_prev)
  tot <- data.table(
    location     = "Total (selected countries)",
    dd_current   = sum(bt$dd_current,   na.rm = TRUE),
    base_current = sum(bt$base_current, na.rm = TRUE),
    dd_prev      = sum(bt$dd_prev,      na.rm = TRUE),
    base_prev    = sum(bt$base_prev,    na.rm = TRUE))
  tot[, `:=`(pct_current = dd_current / base_current,
             pct_prev    = dd_prev    / base_prev,
             ratio       = dd_current / dd_prev)]
  bt_all <- rbind(bt, tot, fill = TRUE)

  bt_fmt <- bt_all[, .(
    Country                              = location,
    `Current: deaths delayed (M)`        = fmt_m(dd_current, 3),
    `Current: % of baseline`             = fmt_pct(pct_current, 2),
    `Previous 30%: deaths delayed (M)`   = fmt_m(dd_prev, 3),
    `Previous 30%: % of baseline`        = fmt_pct(pct_prev, 2),
    `Current ÷ previous`                 = formatC(ratio, format = "f", digits = 2)
  )]

  kable(bt_fmt,
        caption = paste0("Table 4. Benchmark — current full package vs. the ",
                         "100 Million Lives Saved 30% population sodium-reduction ",
                         "estimate, ", impact_window, ", ", nrow(bt),
                         " selected countries."),
        align = c("l", rep("r", 5))) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = TRUE, font_size = 13) |>
    add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Current model (full package)" = 2,
                       "Previous model (30% sodium)" = 2, " " = 1)) |>
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
    row_spec(nrow(bt_fmt), bold = TRUE, background = "#eef2f7") |>
    footnote(general = paste0(
      "Previous-model figures: UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx (sheet ",
      "'Location And Cause', intervention 'Population Sodium Reduction'). ",
      "'% of baseline' is each model's deaths delayed relative to ITS OWN ",
      "baseline CVD deaths, which is the more comparable metric because the ",
      "two models use different baselines and horizons. This is a contextual ",
      "comparison: the previous scenario applies a uniform 30% sodium cut, ",
      "whereas the full package applies source-limited policy effects, so the ",
      "current total is expected to be lower."))
} else {
  cat("Benchmark workbook unavailable; Table 4 skipped.\n")
}
```

## Figure 7 — Deaths delayed by country: full package vs. 30% sodium reduction

```{r benchmark-fig, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
if (benchmark_available) {
  p_bench <- ggplot(bench_long,
                    aes(dd / 1e6, reorder(location, dd), fill = model)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.78)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = fmt_m(dd, 2)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
              hjust = -0.1, size = 2.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = bench_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.16)), labels = comma) +
    labs(title = paste0("Deaths delayed: current full package vs. previous 30% ",
                        "sodium reduction"),
         subtitle = paste0(length(sel_countries), " selected countries; ",
                          impact_window, "; all CVD causes"),
         x = "Deaths delayed (millions)", y = NULL,
         caption = paste0("Previous = 100 Million Lives Saved, 'Population Sodium ",
                          "Reduction' (30% intake cut). Contextual comparison; ",
                          "scenarios and horizons are not fully equivalent.")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  print(p_bench)

  cat("Benchmark workbook unavailable; Figure 7 skipped.\n")

```

**Interpretation.** The two models rank the selected countries similarly —
China and India dominate the absolute deaths delayed under both, tracking their
share of the regional CVD burden. The **previous flat-30% scenario delays more
deaths** than the current full package in essentially every country, consistent
with its larger (uniform) exposure change; the current package's benefit is
bounded by how much of each country's sodium its four policies can actually
reach. Where the current package closes much of the gap (a higher
current ÷ previous ratio), local intake is concentrated in the **packaged**
source that FOPL, salt targets and fiscal policy jointly target. Because the
scenarios and horizons are **not fully equivalent**, these numbers should be
read as a **contextual cross-check** on order of magnitude and country ranking,
not as a validation target.

---

# Limitations and interpretation

- **Deaths delayed, not averted (sodium→SBP policies).** For public procurement,
  FOPL, salt targets, fiscal, and the **primary Na/K→SBP LSS** method, case
  fatality is held at baseline, so these lower incidence and shift mortality
  later; cumulative totals depend on the accounting window. Only the optional
  **SSaSS trial-RR benchmark** lowers stroke case fatality (averting, not only
  delaying, some stroke deaths).
- **NCD-RisC eligibility is age-standardised 30–79, not age-specific.** The
  diagnosed/treated population shares that size LSS scenarios 4/5 are single
  age-standardised values applied across all modelled ages, and the **post-2019
  proportions are carried forward** unchanged. This misstates eligibility at the
  age extremes and ignores any post-2019 diagnosis/treatment gains.
- **LSS uptake and adherence are uncertain.** Uptake (adoption among the eligible)
  and adherence (SSaSS yr-5 ≈ 0.92) are assumptions; the whole-population coverage
  (s2) is a manual toggle. Household spillover is not modelled.
- **K→SBP evidence is sparser than Na→SBP, and additivity is assumed.** The
  potassium channel uses the Filippini (2020) achieved-excretion dose-response
  with unit-conversion assumptions (39.1 mg/mmol; intake→excretion ÷1.3) and a
  baseline-sodium modulation; the sodium- and potassium-mediated SBP changes are
  **assumed additive** (a factor lets this be relaxed). The K evidence base is
  thinner than for sodium.
- **LSS is benefit-only — no hyperkalaemia/CKD harm channel.** Unlike Huang et
  al., this disease model has no CKD state, so LSS benefits are **not offset** by
  potential renal harms. LSS effects should be read as upper-ish estimates in
  populations where hyperkalaemia risk matters.
- **Baseline potassium** is from Reddin 2023 with a **region-mean fallback** for
  countries absent from the source (Viet Nam → Southeast Asia; Ethiopia → Eastern
  Sub-Saharan Africa), so those two rest on regional, not national, data.
- **Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS applicability.** The two LSS methods are not
  interchangeable: SSaSS RRs apply only to SSaSS-comparable (diagnosed/treated
  HTN) populations and stroke outcomes, whereas Na/K–SBP covers all four causes
  via SBP. They are reported side by side, never combined, and no single pathway
  drives a cause twice.
- **hstroke incidence quirk (pre-existing).** All sodium→SBP scenarios (including
  Na/K–SBP LSS) inherit a known disease-model decomposition quirk that inflates
  hemorrhagic-stroke *incidence* effects; the SSaSS benchmark path was corrected
  for it, but fixing the root cause is out of scope here.
- **Euromonitor trend: category definitions, extrapolation, composition-only.**
  The packaged trend uses Matti's pre-combined v002 category set; the post-2030
  rule (`r RC$euromonitor$post2030`) and the ceiling
  (`r fmt_pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling,0)`) are **extrapolation assumptions**, and
  the trend reweights *composition* only — total sodium intake is held fixed.
- **Fiscal policy is exploratory.** Pass-through, own-price elasticity, taxable
  share and substitution are uncertain and applying broad-category elasticities
  to high-sodium foods is contested; fiscal results are provisional, not
  confirmed. Its package membership follows `include_fiscal_in_package`.
- **Uncertainty not fully propagated.** Effect sizes, coverage, K→SBP anchors and
  the Euromonitor growth CI are largely used as point estimates; no probabilistic
  sensitivity analysis is run (the fiscal and Euromonitor CIs are shown but not
  propagated into deaths-delayed).
- **Source shares** for the ten prioritised countries are documented but several
  (notably Nigeria/Cameroon, with Nigeria a proxy for Cameroon) are provisional;
  any country outside the set falls back to the `default` (mean) profile. Public
  procurement uses a stale school-inclusive 5% share pending adults-only inputs.
- **Independent-cause structure.** The four causes share one population but are
  modelled independently, so "all-cause" prevalence/incidence sum cause-specific
  cases and may count comorbid individuals more than once.

---

# Deck artifacts (slide-deck export) {#deck-export}

This final section exists purely to hand computed elements to the Beamer slide
deck `docs/UWRTSL-sodium-policy.Rmd`. **All computation for the deck happens
here** (the deck itself performs none): every figure is written as a PNG and
every table/number is written into a single `deck_data.rds` bundle. The deck
loads that bundle and includes the PNGs, so the two documents can never drift.
Artifacts are written to `docs/deck_assets/`.

```{r deck-export, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ---- Output location --------------------------------------------------------
deck_dir <- file.path(wd, "docs", "deck_assets")
dir.create(deck_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_fig <- function(plot, name, w, h) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(filename = file.path(deck_dir, name), plot = plot,
                  width = w, height = h, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  invisible(name)
}

# Pre-render a data.frame to a booktabs LaTeX tabular, wrapped in \resizebox so
# it can never overflow a 16:9 Beamer frame. escape = TRUE handles %, & etc.
mk_tex <- function(df, align = NULL) {
  if (is.null(align)) align <- c("l", rep("r", ncol(df) - 1L))
  body <- knitr::kable(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = align,
                       linesep = "", escape = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
  paste0("\\resizebox{\\textwidth}{!}{%\n", as.character(body), "\n}")
}

  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

  geom_tile(data = boxes, aes(x = x, y = 1), width = 0.84, height = 0.7,
            fill = "#e8eef4", color = "#1f78b4", linewidth = 0.6) +

# ---- FIG: LSS Na/K causal pathway (deck Slide A) ----------------------------
mk_flow <- function(labels, fill = "#e8f2ea", border = "#59A14F") {
  n <- length(labels)
  bx <- data.table(x = seq_len(n), label = labels)
  ar <- data.table(x = (seq_len(n - 1)) + 0.44, xend = (2:n) - 0.44, y = 1, yend = 1)
  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1), width = 0.86, height = 0.7,
              fill = fill, color = border, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1, label = label), size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.95) +
    geom_segment(data = ar, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed"),
                 linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey30") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, n + 0.5), ylim = c(0.55, 1.45)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12)
}

  "↓ CVD incidence\nall 4 causes (via SBP)",

  lss_harms        = RC$lss$harms_modelled,
  lss_cov_all      = fmt_pct(RC$lss$coverage_all, 0),
  htn_dx_pop       = fmt_pct(mean(.he$diagnosed_pop, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
  htn_tx_pop       = fmt_pct(mean(.he$treated_pop,   na.rm = TRUE), 0),
  htn_source_year  = RC$htn_source_year,
  # SSaSS benchmark constants (surfaced for the benchmark section only)
  lss_rr_stroke_inc = formatC(LSS_RR_STROKE_INC, format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_cf_mult       = formatC(LSS_CF_MULT,       format = "f", digits = 3),
  lss_stroke_total  = formatC(LSS_STROKE_TOTAL,  format = "f", digits = 2),
  # applied per-source effect sizes (from the published intervention_effects)
  eff_public       = fmt_pct(eff_of("public_procurement", "public"), 0),
  eff_fopl         = fmt_pct(eff_of("fopl", "packaged"), 1),
  eff_salttargets  = fmt_pct(eff_of("salt_targets", "packaged"), 0),
  eff_fiscal       = fmt_pct(RC$fiscal$base_effect, 0),
  # fiscal pathway (EXPLORATORY) from fiscal_audit base row
  fiscal_status        = "exploratory",
  fiscal_tax_rate      = fmt_pct(RC$fiscal$base$tax_rate, 0),
  fiscal_taxable_share = fmt_pct(RC$fiscal$base$taxable_share, 0),
  fiscal_in_package    = as.character(RC$fiscal$include_in_package),
  # fiscal pathway detail (EXPLORATORY) — base row + low/high, from fiscal_audit
  fiscal_pass_through  = fmt_pct(fa_base$pass_through, 0),
  fiscal_elasticity    = formatC(fa_base$elasticity, format = "f", digits = 2),
  fiscal_price_change  = fmt_pct(fa_base$price_change, 0),
  fiscal_qty_response  = fmt_pct(abs(fa_base$quantity_response), 0),
  fiscal_taxed_pkg_red = fmt_pct(fa_base$taxed_packaged_reduction, 0),
  fiscal_pkg_red       = fmt_pct(fa_base$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_substitution  = fmt_pct(fa_base$substitution, 0),
  fiscal_reformulation = fmt_pct(fa_base$reformulation, 0),
  fiscal_low_pkg       = fmt_pct(fa_low$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_high_pkg      = fmt_pct(fa_high$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_low_m         = fmt_m(ddc("fiscal_low"), 2),
  fiscal_high_m        = fmt_m(ddc("fiscal_high"), 2),
  # LSS Na/K→SBP detail (representative means over whole-population s2 rows)
  lss_uptake           = formatC(RC$lss$uptake, format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_nonhtn_factor    = formatC(RC$lss$nonhtn_factor, format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_eff_na_k_disc    = fmt_pct(RC$lss$eff_lss_na_k_discretionary, 0),
  lss_k_mg_per_mmol    = as.character(RC$lss$k_mg_per_mmol),
  lss_k_intake_excr    = as.character(RC$lss$k_intake_to_excretion),
  lss_dsbp_na          = formatC(mean(la_dk$sbp_delta_na_mmHg,       na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_dsbp_k           = formatC(mean(la_dk$sbp_delta_k_mmHg,        na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_dsbp_tot         = formatC(mean(la_dk$sbp_delta_combined_mmHg, na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_na_disp          = formatC(mean(la_dk$sodium_displaced_g,      na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_k_add            = formatC(mean(la_dk$potassium_added_g,       na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  # published media effect (retained in registry; excluded from reported scenarios)
  eff_media            = fmt_pct(eff_of("media_campaign", "packaged"), 0),
  # external comparators (documented in the report layer, not our pipeline output)
  huang_s2_deaths      = "1.85 million/year",
  saxena_na_red        = "≈100 mg/day (≈10%)",
  saxena_tax           = "20%",
  saxena_horizon       = "20 years",
  eff_lss          = fmt_pct(eff_of("lss", "discretionary"), 0),
  vn_sanity        = formatC(vn_sanity, format = "f", digits = 4),
  # PROVISIONAL: public-procurement share is still the stale school-inclusive 5%.
  public_share     = fmt_pct(source_shares[location == "Viet Nam", public], 1),
  # Euromonitor packaged-food trend (v002 combined) summary stats
  euro_window      = RC$euromonitor$window,
  euro_ceiling     = fmt_pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling, 0),
  euro_post2030    = RC$euromonitor$post2030,
  pkg_apc_median   = pkg_apc_median,
  pkg_apc_range    = pkg_apc_range,
  # worked composition example: FOPL + salt targets on 'packaged'
  compose_fopl_salt = fmt_pct(1 - (1 - eff_of("fopl","packaged")) * (1 - eff_of("salt_targets","packaged")), 1),
  # SSaSS / LSS composition constants
  ssass_na_mgday   = "-350 mg/day",
  ssass_base_gday  = "4.3 g/day",
  ssass_sbp_mmhg   = "-3.34 mmHg",
  ssass_k_mgday    = "+803 mg/day",
  lss_ratio        = paste0(fmt_pct(RC$lss$nacl_fraction,0), " NaCl / ", fmt_pct(RC$lss$kcl_fraction,0), " KCl"),
  # benchmark vs the 100 Million Lives Saved 30% population sodium reduction
  bench_n          = length(sel_countries),
  bench_current_m  = if (benchmark_available) fmt_m(bench_cur_tot, 2)  else "n/a",
  bench_prev_m     = if (benchmark_available) fmt_m(bench_prev_tot, 2) else "n/a",
  bench_ratio      = if (benchmark_available)
                       formatC(bench_ratio_tot, format = "f", digits = 2) else "n/a"
)

# LaTeX-safe percent signs. The deck inlines these nums both in markdown text
# (where pandoc would escape a bare '%') AND inside raw-LaTeX environments
# (tabular / itemize / block) where it would NOT -- an unescaped '%' there
# becomes a comment and silently eats the rest of the line. Pre-escaping every
# '%' to '\%' is correct in both contexts, so it is done once here.
nums <- lapply(nums, function(v)
  if (is.character(v)) gsub("%", "\\\\%", v, perl = TRUE) else v)

# ---- NEW deck artifacts (Task 4i): year-specific shares, LSS Na/K pathway, ---
# NCD-RisC eligibility, Na/K-vs-SSaSS, fiscal audit. Guarded so a skipped chunk
# never breaks the bundle.
if (exists("fig_pkg_time")) save_fig(fig_pkg_time, "fig_packaged_time.png", 10, 5)
tex_ncd_eligibility <- if (exists("he_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(he_tbl),
  align = c("l","l", rep("r",6))) else "\\emph{NCD-RisC eligibility unavailable.}"
tex_lss_audit <- if (exists("la_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(la_tbl),
  align = c("l","l", rep("r",8))) else "\\emph{LSS audit unavailable.}"
tex_fiscal_audit <- if (exists("fa_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(fa_tbl),
  align = c("l", rep("r",10))) else "\\emph{Fiscal audit unavailable.}"
tex_nak_ssass <- if (exists("cmp_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(cmp_tbl),
  align = c("l","l","l", rep("r",5))) else "\\emph{Na/K-vs-SSaSS comparison unavailable.}"
tex_fiscal_sensitivity <- if (exists("fr_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(fr_tbl),
  align = c("l","r","r")) else "\\emph{Fiscal sensitivity results unavailable.}"
tex_huang_ours  <- if (exists("huang_cmp"))  mk_tex(huang_cmp,  align = c("l","l","l")) else "\\emph{Huang comparison unavailable.}"
tex_saxena_ours <- if (exists("saxena_cmp")) mk_tex(saxena_cmp, align = c("l","l","l")) else "\\emph{Saxena comparison unavailable.}"

figs <- list(
  source_shares = "fig_source_shares.png",
  salteff       = "fig_salteff.png",
  salteff_pkg   = "fig_salteff_pkg.png",
  flow          = "fig_flow.png",
  baseline_asmr = "fig_baseline_asmr.png",
  incidence     = "fig_incidence.png",
  deaths        = "fig_deaths.png",
  results_bar   = "fig_results_bar.png",
  bycause       = "fig_bycause.png",
  countries     = "fig_countries.png",
  benchmark      = "fig_benchmark.png",
  packaged_time  = "fig_packaged_time.png",  # NEW: packaged share over time by country
  lss_pathway    = "fig_lss_pathway.png",    # NEW: LSS Na/K causal pathway
  fiscal_pathway = "fig_fiscal_pathway.png"  # NEW: fiscal tax->price->demand->sodium pathway
)

tex <- list(
  effect_sizes    = tex_effect_sizes,
  salteff         = tex_salteff,
  source_shares   = tex_source_shares,
  packaged_trend  = tex_packaged_trend,
  results         = tex_results,
  benchmark       = tex_benchmark,
  ncd_eligibility = tex_ncd_eligibility,   # NEW (Task 4i)
  lss_audit       = tex_lss_audit,         # NEW
  fiscal_audit    = tex_fiscal_audit,      # NEW
  nak_vs_ssass    = tex_nak_ssass,         # NEW
  fiscal_sensitivity = tex_fiscal_sensitivity,  # NEW: deaths delayed low/base/high
  huang_ours      = tex_huang_ours,        # NEW: LSS vs Huang et al. 2026
  saxena_ours     = tex_saxena_ours        # NEW: fiscal vs Saxena et al. 2025
)

deck <- list(nums = nums, figs = figs, tex = tex)
saveRDS(deck, file = file.path(deck_dir, "deck_data.rds"))

message("Deck artifacts written to: ", deck_dir)
message("  figures: ", paste(unlist(figs), collapse = ", "))
message("  bundle : deck_data.rds")
```
